en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Nineteenth Chapter
The Discourse on the Fruits of Recluseship:
Is the fruit of recluseship unconditioned? Yes.
Is Nibbāna a refuge, a shelter, a resort, the ultimate goal, the undecaying, and the deathless?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the fruit of recluseship unconditioned, and is Nibbāna unconditioned?
“Yes.
“Are there two unconditioned things?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Are there two unconditioned things?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
“Does the intermediate space blow?
“One should not say so.
… [as before] … “Is the fruit of recluseship unconditioned (asaṅkhata)?”
“Yes,” [you reply].
“Then is recluseship unconditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the state of recluseship conditioned?
Yes. Is the fruit of the state of recluseship conditioned? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the fruit of stream-entry unconditioned? Yes.
Is the path of stream-entry unconditioned?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is the path of stream-entry conditioned?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the fruit of stream-entry conditioned?
You should not say so … [and so on] … up to … .
Is the fruit of once-returning …pe… the fruit of non-returning …pe… the fruit of arahantship unconditioned?
“Yes.
“Then is the path of arahantship unconditioned?
“It should not be said so…” [and so on].
Is the path to arahantship conditioned? Yes.
Is the fruit of arahantship conditioned?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … The fruit of stream-entry is unconditioned; the fruit of once-returning … [as before] … the fruit of non-returning … [as before].
Is the fruit of arahantship unconditioned, and Nibbāna unconditioned?
Yes. Are there five unconditioned things?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … that there are five unconditioned things? Yes.
"Are there five refuges...
[as before] ...or is there an interval?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
The Discourse on the Fruits of the Ascetic Life is finished.
